description:
Turns the claim and recovery free functions into a `claims()` executor facade, so the CLI's claim and recover arms call the executor instead of passing a storage handle into `commands::claim`.

## Background

Claims are the one command family outside `CommandExecutor`. `crates/jit/src/commands/claim.rs` exposes free functions that take `&storage` and `&WorktreePaths` explicitly: `execute_claim_acquire`, `execute_claim_heartbeat`, `execute_claim_release_by_issue`, `execute_claim_renew`, `execute_claim_status`, `execute_claim_list`, `execute_claim_force_evict` and `execute_recover`, with bounds ranging from none to `IssueStore + RepositoryStateStore`. The `Commands::Claim` arms and the `Commands::Recover` arm of `crates/jit/src/main.rs` (or their handler module under `crates/jit/src/dispatch/`) import these functions and pass `&storage` and the worktree paths the executor already holds. That is a storage call the CLI makes on its own, and it leaves claims outside the narrow-capability scheme every other family follows: `CommandExecutor::<family>()` returns a borrowing facade (`IssueOps<'_, S>` and its peers) whose methods use the executor's storage and worktree paths.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `CommandExecutor::claims` returns a `ClaimOps<'_, S>` facade whose methods perform acquire, heartbeat, release-by-issue, renew, status, list, force-evict and recover, taking their storage and worktree paths from the executor.
- [hard] REQ-02: The CLI's claim and recover command paths call `claims()` methods and pass no storage handle or worktree paths, and `commands::claim` exports no public `execute_*` free function.
- [hard] REQ-03: Claim and recover output, exit codes and lease behaviour are unchanged: the existing claim, lease and recovery suites pass with no assertion weakened.

## Notes

- Methods keep the per-function storage bounds as bounds on their facade impl blocks; operations that need no storage still read worktree paths from the executor.
- Recovery's session ordering (claim coordination before the operation session) is behaviour this work preserves, not changes.
- Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md` (D-1, D-11); method inventory: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/investigation.md` area 3.
title: Claim and recover operations behind a claims facade
